newsitem.title: UK: European bonds rise, bourses slip ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: European bonds rise, bourses slip ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: European bond markets rallied strongly on Thursday but the glow came off share markets as investors took profits ahead of potentially-troubling U.S. payrolls figures due on Friday.
London's blue chip FTSE 100 share index popped up to a fresh trading high of 4,024.3 in early trade before sliding back below the 4,000 watershed it crossed for the first time on Wednesday.
French stocks also fell, but bond markets jumped in tandem with this week's rally in U.S. Treasuries.
Italian bonds soared to new peaks, boosted by the decision of the Bank of Spain to shave half a percentage point off Spain's main money market rate, making Italian bonds more attrative.

French and British government bonds, or gilts, also rallied strongly, although traders said Friday's U.S. data could prompt profit-taking by investors fearful the numbers could point towards an interest rate rise in coming weeks.
"We were looking for gilts to rally over the past week, and they have done. But this morning things have really gone berserk," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Grundy in London.
With German markets closed for the country's reunification holiday, foreign exchange markets were relatively quiet.
Gold eased further and aluminium slumped to a 2-1/4 year low on the London Metal Exchange, with higher supplies meeting declining demand in Europe.
The dollar kept to narrow ranges against the mark and yen during the European morning, with trade cautious ahead of Friday's payrolls data.
"People are wary about taking the dollar higher ahead of tomorrow, especially when you consider the extreme reaction the payrolls numbers can generate," said a Swiss bank dealer.
"There is still a big question mark over which way the dollar will travel if the figures are outside expectations."
Talk of capital flowing out of Japan kept the yen depressed but analysts remained cautious.

"The funding of carry trades by speculative players is perhaps a more convincing rationalisation of continued yen weakness," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
By 1100 GMT the dollar was quoted around 111.39 yen and 1.5319 marks versus Wednesday's late European levels of 111.75 and 1.5277.
Wall Street's fresh record overnight was not enough to keep European equity markets up at Wednesday's peaks.
In London, the equity futures market led the FTSE index lower after its early spurt.
"We ran into a bit of profit-taking, but nothing has changed," said one trader. "The main reasons the UK market (has been) up is because there's a lot of cash around and gilts are strong."

Topping London's most active list were shares in shipping group P&O, up 12p to 637p after news it would merge its ferry business on short Channel routes between France and Britain with those of Swedish rival Stena Line.
In Paris, French shares trimmed opening gains as the market consolidated Wednesday's 0.88 percent rise and the October CAC future slipped.
Food group Bongrain fell 195 francs to 2,150 by 1100 GMT after reporting its first-half profit dropped 21 percent.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar traded around 111.39 yen and 1.5319 marks versus Wednesday's late European levels of 111.75 and 1.5277.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was down 19.8 points at 3,995.3.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 11.56 points at 2,130.28.
Frankfurt - The market was closed for a holiday. The 30-share DAX index closed on Wednesday at 2,676.5.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.50 against $380.35 previously with no follow through to Wednesday's short-covering rally. Silver was unchanged $4.92.
